channel.title: The Awesome Ledger — awesome-webgl
channel.description: New entries across the GitHub awesome ecosystem, diffed nightly.

item.title: Building a Browser Solar System Explorer with NASA Data and Raw WebGL2 — via awesome-webgl
item.description: Engineering case study on rendering the Space Simulator Online 3D Solar System, Milky Way, and 6,000+ NASA exoplanets at 60 FPS using raw WebGL 2 shaders without Three.js.

item.title: zephyr3d — via awesome-webgl
item.description: A TypeScript-based 3D rendering engine with WebGPU/WebGL support.

item.title: textmode.js — via awesome-webgl
item.description: Lightweight, framework-agnostic creative coding library for real-time ASCII and textmode graphics using WebGL2.

item.title: leaflet-webgl-markers — via awesome-webgl
item.description: Leaflet plugin for rendering millions of point markers on a single WebGL canvas, with FBO picking and zero redraw while dragging.

item.title: img2threejs — via awesome-webgl
item.description: Toolkit that rebuilds the object in a reference image as a code-only, procedural Three.js model - primitives, procedural shaders, generated geometry, no downloaded meshes.

item.title: encantar.js — via awesome-webgl
item.description: GPU-accelerated Augmented Reality library that works on any device (iOS, Android, desktops). Easy to use and requires no WebXR support.

item.title: dither-flow — via awesome-webgl
item.description: Cursor-stirred 1-bit dithered flow field, WebGL 2 only, zero dependencies.

item.title: Zero Bytes of Geometry: A Metal Lattice Sphere-Traced in a 14.9 KB Page — via awesome-webgl
item.description: Ray marching a signed distance field in raw WebGL 2, with an analytic environment in place of an HDR file and resolution adapted against the display refresh period.

item.title: WorldSeed — via awesome-webgl
item.description: Turns open geospatial data into playable, exportable Three.js worlds with terrain-aware roads, GLB, road graphs, spawn points, and versioned JSON Schema.

item.title: Web3D Viewer — via awesome-webgl
item.description: Single-file OBJ viewer that logs how every MTL texture reference was resolved (exact path, extension-stripped, fuzzy) and which ones failed, so missing materials are traceable instead of silently rendering black.

item.title: Vysmo Transitions — via awesome-webgl
item.description: Tree-shakable WebGL 2 library of 60 endpoint-correct transitions with mesh and multi-pass support, ~5 KB gzipped.

item.title: TutorialSearch — via awesome-webgl
item.description: Free cross-platform search engine indexing 50,000+ tutorials from Udemy, Skillshare, Pluralsight, and other major learning platforms across 45+ categories.

item.title: TradeCanvas — via awesome-webgl
item.description: Financial charting library that draws candles, indicators and depth heatmaps with WebGL 2, falling back to Canvas 2D.

item.title: Speedy Vision — via awesome-webgl
item.description: GPU-accelerated Computer Vision library for JavaScript.

item.title: NixieFX — via awesome-webgl
item.description: Particle and VFX runtime for PixiJS and Three.js, authored in a browser-based editor.

item.title: Houdini to Three.js: Testing glTF Compression and Instancing — via awesome-webgl
item.description: Case study of geometry, texture compression and instancing with WebGPU and WebGL2 checks.

item.title: Globedots — via awesome-webgl
item.description: Dot-matrix globe on WebGL2 in 17 kB, with markers, arcs, labels, heat maps, and a day-night line.

item.title: Fast3D — via awesome-webgl
item.description: Browser-based 3D toolbox: convert between GLB, GLTF, OBJ, STL, FBX and PLY, compress models and preview them in a full-featured viewer. Everything runs client-side.

item.title: A tutorial on infinite canvas with WebGL — via awesome-webgl
item.description: A hands-on tutorial for building a GPU-accelerated infinite canvas in the browser, with first-class WebGL support (and WebGPU) via a unified graphics API—covering ECS, SDF-based 2D primitives, GPU text, and tile-based rendering, by @xiaoiver.
